ThingDef.label: AKS Type I
ThingDef.description:
Caliber: 7.62x39mm. 30-round detachable mag. Select-Fire.
The AK (Avtomat Kalashnikova) is a Soviet assault rifle designed between 1946-1947 by Mikhail Kalashnikov. Commonly (and somewhat anachronistically) known as the "AK-47," the AK is one of the most recognizable and widely used weapons platforms ever made, with over 100 million Kalashnikov-type guns having been produced since 1948. Reputed for its ease of mass production and reliability, the AK was the backbone of the Soviet Armed Forces and continues to be the standard service platform in most former Warsaw Pact nations.
The early line of AK rifles consists of three major variants - the Type I (produced from 1948/49 to 1951), Type II (1951-1954/55), and Type III (1955-1959.) Type I AKs had stamped sheet metal receivers, while the subsequent Type II had a milled receiver. The Type III was a further update that lightened the milled receiver. This rifle is a Type I, which was the first to be adopted by the USSR military forces but was replaced after only three years, due to a high rejection rate for newly built guns. Consequently, Type I AKs are much less common than the later variants.
The AKS variant has a metal underfolding stock intended for use by paratroopers and mechanized infantry.
